maya: Quick FYI — ran a profiling sweep on the KV slice mapping experiment (TP + per-layer KV sharding). Seeing unexpected all-reduce spikes around layers 9-13 when sequence length > 1024.
eli: can you paste the perf trace? which kernel/runtime build?
maya: runtime: v1.8.2-kernel-opt + our recent kernel-selection patch. trace excerpt: ```
# perf timeline (ms)
layer8    compute  2.3
layer9    allred   7.8  << spike
layer10   allred   9.2  << spike
layer11   compute  2.9
layer12   allred   8.6
layer13   compute  2.4
total     step     42.1
```
eli: hmm that's a lot for all-reduce. is this the TP placement with KV slices striped across TP ranks? or did you try affinity (hot-slice locality)?
maya: striped across TP ranks by default. I tried quick affinity mapping (co-locate hot KV pages to the same TP rank) — that reduced spike magnitude ~40% for layer9 in a single run but introduced a small imbalance elsewhere.
sam: two hypotheses: (1) our kernel-selection picks a smaller GEMM kernel for the mid layers with long seqs causing extra host->device syncs; (2) the batching heuristic triggers a bigger batch when KV miss rate is high, blowing up all-reduce sizes.
noah: +1 on the batching angle. saw similar in the 1.8.0 -> 1.8.2 window where we tuned batching aggressiveness. perf-bot: regression alert: "all-reduce 95p latency increased" triggered 3h ago on dedicated-prod cluster-3 (ticket #4567).
maya: repro script I used: ```bash
# repro (toy)
python run_kv_shard_bench.py --model gptx-8b --tp 2 --pp 1 --kv-shard stripe --seq 1280 --batch 4 --kernel-policy auto
```
eli: can you run with `--kernel-policy prefer-large-gemm` and `--kv-shard locality-hot`? compare nvprof traces. also try `--batch=2` to see batching effect.
maya: running now, will post nvprof diffs in a min.
(2m later)
maya: quick results: switch to prefer-large-gemm drops layer10 allred from 9.2 -> 5.1ms; locality-hot mapping drops another ~30%. batch=2 reduces total step by ~12% but increases per-token variance.
sam: sounds like two levers: kernel selection and KV placement. if we can make kernel selection aware of seq length + kv-shard layout we might pick larger kernels when we detect heavy all-reduce loads.
noah: agree. also consider moving small all-reduces to NCCL tree O(1) vs ring if payload small — did we change algorithm recently?
eli: NCCL algorithm is still auto; we can force `nccl_coll_algo=tree` in env for test. try that.
maya: tried tree — reduced tail in one config but increased average in another. looks dependent on payload size.
perf-bot: note saved run artifacts to s3://redwood-perf/artifacts/2100001111/
maya: next steps I'm going to: (1) add a cheap runtime heuristic: if seq > 1024 and kv-shard=stripe -> prefer-large-gemm + locality-hot mapping; (2) add a flag to prefer tree for all-reduces when payload < 256KB; (3) write e2e microbench with batch sweeps and record 95/99p.
sam: also worth adding a lightweight profiler hook to log per-layer all-reduce bytes so we can detect hot layers automatically for affinity.
eli: can we A/B the heuristic in staging (canary 5% traffic) before full rollout? prefer minimal config flags.
maya: yes will prototype and submit PR for v1.8.3. putting notes in the PR that this addresses perf regression #4567.
noah: thanks — ping if you need help with nccl/env testing on dedicated nodes.
eli: if we can get this to reduce 95p by >30% we can mark regression fixed. :thumbsup:
maya: will update with PR link + perf numbers.
(ends)
